about: Shared test cases for reading song titles and artist credits, and for deciding whether two songs are the same recording.
The Octo server (octo/Services/Common/SongIdentity.cs) and the Octo Android app implement the same rules and both run every case in this file, so the two cannot drift apart.
Change a rule in both places and in this file together. Every note says why a case expects what it does.

rules.fold: Unicode NFKC (fullwidth characters become ASCII), curly quotes and dashes made plain, underscores read as spaces, Cyrillic and Greek lookalike letters read as Latin inside a word that also has Latin letters.
rules.titleKey: The title after folding, with a track number in front ('01 - ', '01. ', '1-01 ') and a leading 'Artist - ' removed, brackets read (guests, upload noise, version markers and subtitles are taken out; a part number such as 'Pt. 2' stays), a ' - ' tail that is a version or noise removed, a trailing 'feat. X' removed, and a trailing 'Remix', 'Sped Up', 'Slowed', 'Nightcore', 'Instrumental', 'Acapella', 'Karaoke', 'Drumless' or '8D Audio' read as a version. Then lowercased, 'ss' for 'ß', accents (U+0300 to U+036F and the other combining diacritic blocks) removed, '&' and a spaced '+' read as 'and', and only letters, digits and combining marks kept. A title with no letters or digits keeps its symbols ('🔥', '!!!').
rules.looseKey: The title key again after reading stylized characters as letters: '$' as s and '@' as a when next to a letter, '0' as o and '3' as e when next to a letter and not next to a digit, '!' as i between two letters. Two titles match when either key agrees; the loose key never replaces the exact one.
rules.versions: Canonical marker names found in brackets, in a ' - ' tail, or as a trailing word: live, remix, mix, dub, edit, radio edit, extended, acoustic, instrumental, acapella, demo, sped up, slowed, reverb, nightcore, vip, bootleg, rework, unplugged, session, reprise, cover, karaoke, drumless, 8d, piano, orchestral (also 'symphonic'), lofi, bass boosted, mashup, medley, megamix, blend, clean, version, and the neutral ones remaster, explicit, original, album version, single version, mono, stereo. Neutral markers never make a different recording; every other marker must agree on both sides, or the verdict is 'version'. An edition that changes what is played is a marker ('Drumless Edition', 'Piano Version', '8D Audio'); two songs or more in one ('Mash-Up', 'Medley', 'Mega Mix', 'Blend') is a marker too, and a megamix is never also a mix; a release edition is the same recordings packaged again and no marker at all: deluxe, super deluxe, expanded, anniversary (also '10th Anniversary'), special, collector's, limited, tour or platinum, alone or with 'Edition' or 'Version', and 'Bonus Track' or 'Bonus Tracks', alone or with 'Edition' or 'Version'.
rules.artists: The credit split on , & ; / 、 × x and with feat ft featuring vs presents, never inside a known name ('Tyler, The Creator', 'Earth, Wind & Fire', 'AC/DC', 'Simon & Garfunkel') and never before 'the' after '&' or 'and' ('Bob Marley & The Wailers'). The whole credit is kept as a candidate beside its parts. A bracket in a credit is dropped ('Ye (侃爷)', 'Nirvana (US)'), except that '(feat. X)' adds a guest. ' - Topic' and a 'VEVO' suffix are channel names, not the artist. A leading 'The' is optional. A small alias table maps renamed artists ('Ye' to Kanye West).
rules.same: Two songs are 'same' when the title keys (or loose keys, or the same letters with overlapping numbers) agree, the non-neutral version markers agree, remixers agree when both name one, subtitles agree when both have one, a primary artist of one side is credited on the other, the guests do not conflict (each side naming a guest the other lacks, ignoring names in a non-Latin script), and known lengths are within 3 seconds. 'version' is the same song in a different version, with different guests, or with lengths too far apart. 'different' is anything else, including a missing artist on either side.
rules.isrc: Read first. An ISRC is normalised by uppercasing and removing hyphens, dots and spaces; what is left must match ^[A-Z]{2}[A-Z0-9]{3}[0-9]{7}$ or it is treated as absent. When both sides carry a valid ISRC and any one is on both, the verdict is 'same' at confidence 1 with the reason 'same ISRC', whatever the titles and artists say. When both carry ISRCs and none is shared, that is not a rejection (a re-release or a remaster often gets a new code): the comparison falls through to the rules above exactly as if neither had one.

fields.compare: a and b are {title, artist, seconds?, isrc?}. isrc, optional on either side, is one ISRC as a string or several as a list of strings; a file written before it existed has none and compares exactly as it always did. expect is same, version or different. options, when present, is {lengthToleranceSeconds (null to ignore lengths; default 3), extrasMustAgree (default false), alsoNeutral (markers this caller treats as neutral)}.
fields.parse: input is {title, artist}. expectTitleKey and expectLooseKey are the keys above. expectVersions is every marker found, sorted. expectArtists is the exact key of each artist in order: the split credit first (primary artist first), then guests from brackets in the credit, then guests from the title.
fields.queries: input is {title, artist}. expect is the ordered list of free-text queries (artist, a space, then title): the original; without brackets, guests and version tails; with stylized characters read as letters; the primary artist only; the title alone. A query equal to an earlier one is left out.
